newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Blair makes final appeal to voters.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Blair makes final appeal to voters.

text.p: Tony Blair, bidding to lead his Labour party to power for the first time in 18 years, made a final appeal on Wednesday to British voters to trust him and vote for change in Thursday's general election.

Blair has retained a commanding opinion poll lead over the ruling Conservatives throughout the six-week campaign but he stuck doggedly to his mantra against complacency as he set out on a final gruelling day of campaigning.

"We will not stop trying to persuade people to put their trust in Labour. Between now and when the polls close tomorrow night we will strive for every vote, in every corner of the country," he told an eve-of-poll news conference.

"Because this election is not going to be decided by opinion polls. It is not going to be resolved by pundits. It is in the hands of the British people. Their future is in their hands," the Labour leader said.
"And today I ask them for their trust."
The Labour leader was in relaxed mood, gently shrugging off awkward questions and showing little sign of nerves.
Opinion polls suggest the Labour party, which Blair has dragged into the centre of the political spectrum since taking charge three years ago, is set to win by a landslide.
A running poll in Wednesday's issue of The Daily Telegraph gave them a 20 percentage point lead with a projected majority of 203 seats in the House of Commons (lower house).
Blair repeated his stock promise that Labour's limited but specific commitments, especially in education and health, would make a difference to ordinary peoples' lives.
He said the crucial question of the election was the same as it was six weeks ago. Was Britain as good as it could be or did people deserve better?
"If people think that Britain could be better they should vote for a new and modern Labour party," he said. "So I ask the British people for their support."
